method: Compared all four native connector records to the original PowerPoint-rendered slide 68 and their endpoint IDs in ppt/slides/slide68.xml; shape 13 is GEPOF, 14 is GEPOF+ GREEN and 16 is 10000 POF.

objects.evidenceText: On the 2014 tutorial's conceptual 'Future of POF' plot, the horizontal SPEED axis points right; labeled positions range from 25 Mbps at the left through 1000 Mbps to 10000 Mbps at the right.
objects.reason: The native arrow defines the direction of the conceptual axis; positions are not a measured performance dataset.

objects.evidenceText: On the same conceptual plot, the vertical LENGTH axis points upward, with labels 15 m, 50 m and 100 m at increasing height.
objects.reason: The arrow defines axis direction; no additional limit or tested reach is inferred.

objects.evidenceText: A red curved arrow in the 2014 future-looking diagram leads from the GEPOF cloud toward a '10000 POF' cloud near the 10000 Mbps axis position.
objects.reason: Connector shape 28 attaches native shape 13 (GEPOF) to shape 16 (10000 POF); the arrow represents a proposed direction, not a later proven standard or deployment.

objects.evidenceText: A green upward arrow in the 2014 future-looking diagram leads from the GEPOF cloud toward 'GEPOF+ GREEN' beside the words 'GREEN Light source'.
objects.reason: Connector shape 31 attaches native shape 13 (GEPOF) to shape 14 (GEPOF+ GREEN); the slide presents a future concept rather than a verified performance result.
